promise: The site owner can replace every visible 'WP Sell Services' plugin name with their own brand name across wp-admin menus, page headings, emails, and the frontend dashboard.
ux_bar: After saving a Brand Name AND enabling White Label, the admin menu label, page headings, dashboard header, checkout and login/register pages all show the new name; the Enable toggle being off means a saved brand name changes nothing at all.
notes: Enable toggle gates everything; a brand name alone is inert.

promise: The site owner can set a Primary Color that recolours buttons, badges and accents in both wp-admin and the frontend.
ux_bar: Saving a colour sets --wpss-admin-accent / --wpss-primary on body.wp-admin AND on the frontend containers, so buttons and active-nav borders change on the next load in BOTH places. Semantic status badges (paid/failed) must NOT be recoloured.
notes: Fixed in 1.7.2 (15df02d): previously targeted .wpss-btn-primary while markup uses .wpss-btn--primary, so admin screens never picked up the accent. This row is the regression guard.

promise: The site owner can upload a logo that replaces the plugin's default logo in the dashboard header and in email headers.
ux_bar: Uploading a logo hides .wpss-default-logo and injects the image on dashboard/checkout/login; the same URL reaches every transactional email as header_image, so web and email never show different branding.

promise: The site owner can set a custom email From name and footer text used by every transactional email.

entry_points.admin: Settings > Branding > Email From Name, Email Footer Text

ux_bar: A real sent email shows the configured From name in the inbox and the configured footer at the bottom of the body - verified by sending, not by reading the setting back.

promise: The Hide Branding setting describes exactly what it hides, and does not imply it removes a credit that is already absent.

entry_points.frontend: Dashboard footer (only when a theme re-enables the credit)

ux_bar: The label must not promise an effect the default install cannot show. Free already returns false from wpss_show_powered_by, so on a stock site toggling this changes nothing; the copy has to say so rather than implying an active removal.
notes: Label/effect mismatch fixed in 1.7.2 (8a79b78). Kept as a row because 'setting label overstates its effect' is a recurring defect class.

promise: Recurring services are hidden entirely while renewals cannot collect a payment method, so no owner can switch on a billing flow that would never charge.

entry_points.frontend: MISSING by design - no wizard field, no buyer subscriptions section
entry_points.admin: MISSING by design - no Recurring Services card in Settings > Orders & Disputes; Welcome page shows 'Coming soon' with no Configure link
entry_points.api: routes register but resolve against gated/empty data

roles.admin: cannot enable without a code filter

ux_bar: On a stock install the feature is invisible everywhere - not present-but-broken, not a toggle that silently does nothing. Any release note or doc that describes a recurring-services behaviour must not imply the owner can reach it.
notes: DELIBERATE. is_feature_available() returns apply_filters('wpss_pro_recurring_feature_available', false). Correct product call. audit/FEATURE_AUDIT.md (1.3.1) still lists Recurring Services as a normal shipped subsystem and does not mention the kill switch - the doc is materially wrong. The 1.7.2 changelog initially advertised a fix inside this feature; corrected to a Dev note before release.

promise: When the feature is enabled, the site-wide default billing interval is what pre-selects when a vendor turns on recurring billing.

entry_points.admin: Settings > Orders & Disputes > Recurring Services > Default Billing Interval

ux_bar: After saving a default, the wizard field and the admin metabox both OPEN on that interval - not always Monthly.
notes: Fixed 1.7.2 (abe51d1) via a new public get_default_interval(). Nothing read the setting before, so every field opened on Monthly. Unreachable end-to-end while RECUR-01 is off - a 'saved but not applied' defect hiding inside a hidden feature.

promise: A buyer with an active subscription can pause, resume or cancel it themselves.

entry_points.frontend: Dashboard > My Subscriptions (registered only when the buyer has 1+)

roles.vendor: cannot act on a buyer's subscription

ux_bar: Pause flips the status badge and stops the next cycle immediately; Cancel moves the row out of the active list. A vendor must never see controls for a buyer's subscription.
notes: Unreachable while RECUR-01 is off - a buyer can never accumulate a subscription to manage.

promise: With WooCommerce selected, buyers check out for services through WooCommerce's own cart and checkout.

entry_points.frontend: WooCommerce cart/checkout from a service purchase button

ux_bar: A completed WooCommerce order creates the matching wpss_orders row with platform=woocommerce and the correct platform_fee/vendor_earnings split; the vendor is credited at completion, not at payment.
requires_free: wpss_ecommerce_adapters; StandaloneOrderProvider::mark_as_paid as the single crediting path
notes: Fully active, not beta-gated.

promise: The EDD rail is hidden unless a developer opts in, and when opted in it states plainly what does not work.

entry_points.frontend: MISSING for catalog purchases - Checkout dead-ends. Tips/milestones/extensions do work.
entry_points.admin: Settings > General - EDD appears only when wpss_pro_beta_rails is truthy, marked 'Beta, not purchase-tested'

roles.vendor: cannot rely on it for catalog sales
roles.admin: can opt in via filter only

ux_bar: With the filter off (default) EDD is absent from the platform list entirely. With it on, a persistent admin notice names exactly what breaks: no download created, no refund sync, no pay-order links.
notes: In-admin honesty is good; readme/manifest still list EDD as a shipped adapter without the limitation. Documentation gap.

promise: The FluentCart rail is hidden unless a developer opts in; catalog purchases are not supported on it.

entry_points.admin: Settings > General - only when wpss_pro_beta_rails is truthy

roles.admin: can opt in via filter only

ux_bar: Default install never offers FluentCart. The platform field's description states the beta status and names the filter.
notes: Uses a SECOND namespace wpss-pro/v1 for two routes, unlike every other Pro controller on wpss/v1 - an app client hardcoding wpss/v1 404s on these. Worth a row of its own if the app ever consumes them.

promise: On a WooCommerce site, a buyer paying a milestone phase, tip or paid extension gets a real payable link with no cart to rebuild.

entry_points.frontend: Pay link from notification/dashboard -> WooCommerce checkout-payment URL

ux_bar: The link lands directly on WooCommerce's payment page for a wc-pending order carrying a single fee line; paying it completes the WPSS sub-order and credits the vendor.
notes: MISSING on EDD and FluentCart - the same link falls back to Free's standalone ?pay_order=N URL, which those checkouts do not understand, landing the buyer on an empty cart. Known documented gap.

promise: Refunding a WooCommerce order also reverses the linked tip, milestone and extension sub-orders, not just the parent.
ux_bar: After the refund, every linked sub-order shows refunded/reversed AND the vendor's earnings ledger no longer credits them - checked in the ledger, not only on the order screen.
notes: Previously only the paid handler resolved sub-orders, so a refunded tip was silently ignored while the buyer got their money back. Shared resolver now covers paid/refunded/cancelled/failed.

promise: A site owner can enable Razorpay so buyers pay by UPI/cards/netbanking on the standalone checkout.
ux_bar: Razorpay only offers itself when the toggle is on AND both keys are present - a half-configured gateway is never shown to a buyer. A successful payment's webhook is signature-verified (HMAC-SHA256) and flips the order to paid; a replayed webhook does not double-credit.
notes: 48-hour transient dedup key blocks replay.

promise: On a cart-adapter site the cart owns all payment, so the plugin's own /payments/* routes are deliberately absent.

entry_points.api: MISSING by design - PaymentController registers only when wpss_uses_standalone_payments() is true

roles.buyer: cannot use these endpoints on a cart site

ux_bar: On a WooCommerce/EDD/FluentCart site, GET /wpss/v1/payments/status returns core's rest_no_route 404, not a Pro error. An app client that assumes payments/* always exists breaks silently on a platform switch - the app contract must document this.
notes: Deliberate ('a cart adapter owns ALL payment'). Listed so the mobile-app contract accounts for it.

promise: Only wallet providers that can actually be credited are offered; selecting a retired one warns the owner rather than silently capping every vendor balance at zero.

entry_points.admin: MISSING - there is no Wallet settings tab; the provider choice lives under Payouts

roles.admin: selecting a dead provider gets a warning

ux_bar: Setting the provider to mycred/terawallet/woowallet raises a persistent admin notice explaining balances are being read from the built-in ledger - the vendor's balance must never silently read 0.00.
notes: DOC DRIFT: audit/manifest.json and audit/FEATURE_AUDIT.md list four active providers and a Wallet settings tab. Current source registers ONE provider and there is no Wallet tab. The 1.7.0 removal was deliberate (the layer became read-only, so offering them capped withdrawable balance at 0.00) but the docs were never corrected.

promise: A vendor's withdrawable balance always reflects the plugin's own earnings ledger, even if a previously-configured wallet plugin is deactivated.
ux_bar: Whatever the stored provider option says, the balance resolves to the internal ledger figure - deactivating a third-party wallet plugin never makes a vendor's balance read 0.00.

promise: A site owner can point order deliverables at S3, Google Cloud Storage or DigitalOcean Spaces instead of local media storage.

entry_points.frontend: Delivery download links resolve through the active provider
entry_points.admin: Settings > Advanced > Cloud Storage (provider + credentials + Test Connection)
entry_points.api: MISSING by design - no Pro upload route; uploads go through Free's wpss_store_order_file() seam

roles.vendor: uploads route to the configured provider

ux_bar: Test Connection reports success/failure inline without needing a save first. After saving, the NEXT upload lands in the bucket and the local copy is removed, while files uploaded before the switch keep serving from disk - an existing delivery link must never break because the owner changed provider.
notes: A second, broken Pro upload route was deleted in 1.7.1. Do not reintroduce POST /storage/upload.

promise: If the Pro licence lapses, files already in a bucket stay downloadable while new uploads fall back to local disk.

roles.vendor: new uploads go to local disk

ux_bar: Deactivating the licence then uploading stores locally, while a link to a pre-lapse bucket file still resolves - matching the licence page copy shown to the owner when deactivating.
notes: Deliberate. pre_option_wpss_active_storage_provider forces 'local' when unlicensed.

promise: The site owner gets an Analytics admin page with revenue, orders, top vendors and top services, filterable by period.
ux_bar: Switching the period (Today / 7 / 30 / 90 days / 12 months) redraws charts AND the widget tables without a full page reload, and every option returns figures - none renders blank.
notes: Registers even unlicensed so routes answer 403 wpss_pro_license_required rather than 404 - clients can distinguish 'needs licence' from 'no such route'.

promise: A vendor sees their own views/orders/revenue analytics in their dashboard, filtered by period.
ux_bar: EVERY period option returns a report - including Today. Revenue is NET vendor_earnings and the order count excludes tip sub-orders, so the figures match what the vendor sees in their ledger.
notes: 1.7.2 (ad2d7f0) added 'today' to $valid_periods, the switch AND the match - the match has no default arm, so a missing case returned blank. Enum-drift row: any new period must be added in all three places.

promise: The site owner can export analytics data, capped so a large site cannot hang the request.
ux_bar: An export beyond 10,000 rows returns truncated:true with max_rows:10000 rather than timing out; rows are keyset-paged in batches of 500.
notes: Meets the big-site checklist. Daily cron wpss_pro_cleanup_exports removes stale files.

promise: A vendor can export their own wallet ledger as CSV, matching the on-screen figures exactly.
ux_bar: The CSV's summary block and per-row transactions reconcile to the wallet table on screen, and the export is scoped by user_id so one vendor can never pull another's ledger.

promise: Analytics figures refresh promptly after real activity rather than serving stale cached numbers.
ux_bar: Completing an order bumps the wpss_pro_analytics_ver generation stamp so the very next request recomputes - not a 10-minute wait after real activity.
notes: Generation-stamp invalidation, not a blanket flush.

promise: The site owner can set commission rates by sales volume, category or seller level, applied first-match-wins in priority order.
ux_bar: A qualifying order computes vendor_earnings at the rule's rate instead of the site default, verified against the base-rate maths. Changing a rule must NOT retroactively alter completed orders.
notes: Stripe Connect split reads the PERSISTED computed value rather than recomputing.

promise: The admin can preview a commission rule's effect before saving it.
ux_bar: Preview shows the computed outcome inline WITHOUT persisting the rule - clicking Preview then navigating away must leave no rule behind.

promise: The site owner can enable Stripe Connect Express so vendor payments split automatically at sale time, with vendors onboarding their own bank details.

entry_points.frontend: Dashboard > Payout Methods (not-connected / active / pending-restricted + Onboard)
entry_points.admin: Settings > Payments > Stripe Connect (enable, platform fee %)
entry_points.api: POST wpss/v1/stripe-connect/onboard, GET /status, POST /disconnect; admin: GET /accounts, PUT /settings

roles.admin: can enable, set fee, view all accounts

ux_bar: Onboard redirects to Stripe's hosted flow; on return the card shows the account's REAL Stripe status (Active/Pending/Restricted), not an optimistic 'connected'. A completed sale splits by the configured fee with no manual withdrawal step.

promise: The site owner can batch-pay vendors via PayPal Payouts, and vendors can set their own payout email.

entry_points.frontend: Dashboard > Payout Methods > PayPal email card
entry_points.admin: Settings > Payouts > PayPal Payouts (vendor list + batch action)

roles.vendor: can set own email, cannot trigger a batch

ux_bar: Selecting vendors and confirming submits a REAL PayPal batch that then appears in the batch history with its sync status - never a success message with no batch recorded.
notes: Account deletion keeps batch header rows (owner's record spanning many vendors) and removes only the deleted vendor's item rows and _wpss_paypal_email.

promise: The admin can sync a PayPal batch on demand to see which line items actually paid.
ux_bar: Sync updates each line item to success/failed/pending without waiting for a webhook, and a failed item is visibly distinct from a pending one.

promise: The site owner can charge vendors a recurring membership fee to sell, with plans carrying different service limits.

entry_points.frontend: Dashboard > Subscription (No Subscription / Active / Cancelled-Past Due + pricing table)
entry_points.admin: Settings > Vendor > Vendor Subscriptions (toggle, require-to-sell, plan CRUD)

roles.vendor: can view plans, subscribe, cancel own
roles.admin: can create plans and require subscription

ux_bar: With require-to-sell on, an unsubscribed vendor is blocked from publishing WITH A STATED REASON, and subscribing raises their limit to the plan's max_services immediately. An administrator must never be blocked by the site's own paywall.
notes: Basecamp 10212521285: admins tripped their own paywall seeding demo content. Guard is wpss_member_bypasses_limits() checked first.

promise: The admin can bulk-migrate existing vendors onto a default plan so switching on require-to-sell does not lock out the current vendor base.
ux_bar: After migrating, the 'N vendors have no active subscription' warning count drops to match. On a 2000+ vendor site the migration must batch rather than time out.
notes: UNVERIFIED against the big-site checklist - this is a one-shot bulk write and batching/timeout safety was not confirmed by source read. Worth its own test.

promise: The site owner can configure Firebase so in-app notifications are also delivered as mobile pushes.

entry_points.frontend: n/a - delivered to the companion app
entry_points.admin: Settings > Advanced > Push Notifications (enable + FCM service-account JSON)
entry_points.api: n/a - registration via Free's POST /auth/devices; sending is queued

ux_bar: Valid credentials flip the status line from Off to Sending; the next notification for a device-registered user produces a real FCM v1 push whose title/body match the in-app notification exactly. A half-configured site queues nothing.
requires_free: _wpss_push_devices meta + device-registration routes, which before this feature wrote tokens nothing ever read
notes: Queued via Action Scheduler (group wpss-pro) with WP-Cron fallback - never inline, so 200 notifications in one request cannot block it.

promise: A device that uninstalled the app or rotated its token is forgotten, so sends stop failing against it.
ux_bar: A 404/NOT_FOUND/UNREGISTERED (or a 400 naming the token) prunes ONLY that device; the user's other devices keep receiving. A transient 401/429/5xx must prune nothing.

promise: Pro switches on the buyer tipping feature whose money handling lives entirely in Free.

entry_points.admin: Settings > Commission & Tax > Buyer Tips + tip commission rate
entry_points.api: n/a - reuses Free's tip sub-order path

ux_bar: With Pro active the tip prompt and tip-commission field are visible; unchecking hides the prompt on the next load without touching the money code in Free.
requires_free: the entire tip sub-order create/credit/refund implementation, wpss_tipping_enabled filter
notes: On by default so a site upgrading from a free version that always offered tips does not silently lose it.

promise: A shopper can view prices in another currency as an estimate, while every charge, ledger entry, payout and refund stays in the store's base currency.

entry_points.frontend: Currency switcher on catalog/service pages; price shows base + converted hint

ux_bar: Switching shows an additional approximate hint beside the real base-currency price - never replacing it. Completing a purchase charges and records the BASE currency regardless of the display choice.
notes: A good counter-example to WL-05: the label 'Display Currency' correctly matches its narrow effect.

promise: On WordPress 6.9+, an AI assistant can query marketplace analytics, manage vendor subscription plans and check Stripe Connect config on the admin's behalf.

entry_points.api: Abilities API: Analytics Overview, Manage Vendor Subscriptions, Configure Stripe Connect

ux_bar: Each ability is admin-capability gated in fact, not only in its description. On WP < 6.9 the feature no-ops silently - the owner has NO indicator it is unavailable, which should be fixed or documented.
notes: function_exists('wp_register_ability') guard. The silent no-op is a genuine owner-visibility gap.

promise: The owner can activate/deactivate a licence, and Pro routes answer a distinguishable 403 rather than a generic 404 when unlicensed.

entry_points.api: Pro routes answer 403 wpss_pro_license_required via rest_request_before_callbacks

ux_bar: Deactivating makes a Pro route answer 403 with that code, while a Free-owned route on the same base path keeps working - the gate is per handler class, not per REST base.
requires_free: EDD-SL SDK consolidated in Free's libs/
notes: Licence re-check paused on local/dev so a placeholder key is not invalidated during development.

promise: The License page tells the owner exactly what stops and what keeps working if the licence lapses.

entry_points.admin: License page copy shown above Deactivate

ux_bar: Every item the copy names as KEEPS WORKING and as STOPS must match an actual licence-gated init_*() call in Core\Pro::init() - the list is checked against the code, not trusted.
notes: Cross-checked at enumeration time: copy accurately reflects the gate. Re-check whenever a feature moves in or out of the licensed branch.

promise: A developer can seed or clear demo data across the Pro tables, guarded against production.

entry_points.api: n/a - wp wpss-pro demo, wp wpsspro test:flow

roles.admin: CLI access, gated by Free's CLI Guard

ux_bar: On WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE=production the command refuses without --force; --clear removes only rows this command's own seed log created.
notes: manifest.json previously claimed Pro adds no WP-CLI commands, which kept both write commands out of a guard-hardening sweep (Basecamp 10268057471).

promise: Pro adds exactly one new settings tab (Branding); every other Pro feature nests a card inside an existing Free tab.

entry_points.admin: Settings - Branding is the only new tab; Stripe Connect/Razorpay in Payments, PayPal Payouts in Payouts, Cloud Storage/Push/Display Currency in Advanced, Commission Rules in Commission & Tax, Vendor Subscriptions in Vendor

ux_bar: Only ONE new top-level tab appears. Verifiable by grep: wpss_settings_tabs is used once; every other card uses wpss_settings_sections_*.
notes: DOC DRIFT: audit/FEATURE_AUDIT.md section 5 ('Settings tabs added to FREE (8)') and manifest.json list eight tabs. Only 'branding' registers. 'Wallet' as a tab does not exist; Analytics is a full admin page, not a tab.

promise: Every Configure button on the Welcome-to-Pro page lands on the exact settings section that renders that feature's controls.

entry_points.admin: Sell Services > License > Welcome to Pro

ux_bar: Each Configure button lands on the section that actually renders the card, not a generic tab. A feature with no reachable settings (Recurring) shows 'Coming soon' with NO Configure button rather than a link to an empty screen.
requires_free: wpss_get_settings_url(), which validates against wpss_settings_sections and refuses unknown ids
notes: Fixed in 1.6.0: all ten links previously used a pre-1.3.0 &tab= argument nothing reads, so every button dropped the owner on General, and five named the wrong section.

promise: A buyer on the WooCommerce thank-you page sees what happens next and a link to the matching WPSS order, and the two order screens cross-link.

entry_points.frontend: Woo thank-you panel; WPSS order shows 'WooCommerce Order #N'
entry_points.admin: Woo admin order links to the WPSS order

ux_bar: The cross-link resolves in BOTH directions, including for a sub-order (tip/milestone/extension) whose platform_order_id holds its PARENT's id - the two-key lookup must not leave a sub-order unlinked.
notes: Two keys required: wc_pay_order_id (WPSS meta JSON) and _wpss_pay_order_id (WC meta, HPOS-safe).

promise: The site owner can test email, gateway and storage configuration from the admin before going live.

entry_points.admin: Test Connection / Send Test Email / Test Gateway buttons on the relevant cards

ux_bar: Each test reports success/failure inline using the credentials currently typed, without requiring a save first - so an owner can iterate on a wrong key without persisting it.
notes: Three admin-only AJAX handlers registered directly in Pro::register_hooks(), easy to miss in a per-feature audit because they belong to no single renderer.

promise: Pro removes Free's caps on gallery images, extras, FAQs and requirements in the service wizard.

entry_points.frontend: Service wizard - no cap on those sections

ux_bar: With Pro licensed, adding beyond Free's default cap succeeds because wpss_service_max_gallery/max_extras/max_faq/max_requirements all return -1; with Pro deactivated the caps return and the vendor is told the limit rather than silently losing the extras on save.
notes: DOC/CODE MISMATCH: the class docblock advertises AI title suggestions, service templates, bulk image upload, direct video upload, custom package fields and scheduled publishing. init() wires NONE of them (deferred, Basecamp #10134362181). readme.txt does not sell them, so this is an internal overstatement rather than a customer-facing broken promise - but the docblock should be corrected.

promise: A vendor's public profile carries an analytics teaser block contributed by Pro.
ux_bar: Present and populated when Pro is licensed; absent entirely when unlicensed (the hook registers inside the licensed branch) - never a rendered block with empty or zeroed figures.
notes: UNVERIFIED: the rendered content and CTA of render_vendor_analytics_teaser() were not confirmed from source in the enumeration pass. Needs a browser check.
